A1.justification: Both PDFs describe JOWA and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–F. All 23 pages of each version support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original Atari experiments on multi-game pretraining, model scaling, transfer, and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix F.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and reports revised JOWA-70M results in Table 2.

M1.justification: The VQ-VAE tokenizer, shared transformer, joint world-model and distributional CQL objectives, beam-search planner, and two-stage training procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 15 pretraining games and five held-out Atari games, including the same ablation subsets and expert, suboptimal, and highly-suboptimal fine-tuning scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: MTBC, MGDT, EDT, Scaled-QL, and FICC remain in the main comparisons, with the same scratch-model and MCTS comparisons elsewhere.

E3.justification: Sections 5.1–5.2 and Appendix E retain the same subsampling, model sizes, training budgets, fine-tuning procedures, normalization metrics, and planning settings. No protocol revision accompanies the changed Table 2 values.

E4.justification: Section 5.6 and Appendix F retain the same planning, loss, synthetic-data, Q-head ensemble, task-embedding, data-quality, and emergent-behavior analyses, with unchanged supporting results.

E5.justification: Appendix E.3 still specifies averaging each game score over 16 rollout episodes. Neither version adds training-seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or other uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: A localized revision affects Table 2's JOWA-70M column: 13 per-game returns change, including Atlantis from 570862.5 to 228825 and TimePilot from 3831.3 to 1100.3. Median HNS changes from 0.390 to 0.432 and IQM from 0.476 to 0.485. NameThisGame's best model changes from JOWA-70M to JOWA-150M. Other model columns and all appendix results are unchanged; the PDFs do not explain whether these are corrections or rerun results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, planning derivation, error-bound assumptions, and proofs in Section 4.2 and Appendices A–C are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions concerning joint optimization, planning, scaling, and efficient transfer, including the 78.9% pretraining and 64.7% transfer headline results.

C2.justification: Interpretations of joint optimization, planning, synthetic-data failures, and apparent emergence remain unchanged, as do the computational and per-game scaling limitations. No explanation of the revised JOWA-70M results is added.

D1.justification: Appendix E retains the same architecture specifications, hyperparameters, preprocessing, and implementation instructions. Hardware, training-time disclosures, repository information, and code/checkpoint release statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, bibliography, and positioning relative to prior offline and multi-task RL methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 adds a corresponding-author marker to Yongbin Li and changes the footnote from 'Corresponding author' to 'Equal corresponding author.' The scientific prose and section structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 2 has small spacing changes and updates winner highlighting, notably moving NameThisGame's boldface from JOWA-70M to JOWA-150M. Figures, captions, table organization, and appendix layout are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: Table 2 gains internal consistency: v3's JOWA-70M returns imply a median HNS of about 0.540 and six superhuman games, despite reporting 0.390 and four; v4's revised returns match its reported 0.432 and four. This is a limited improvement in verifiability. However, Section 5.3 and Table 4 still report the old 47.6% IQM rather than Table 2's revised 48.5%, leaving the correction incomplete.
